question: Is deleting the Ascend NPU backend neutral for the CUDA training path?
method: Fold every `device.type == "npu"` / accel.IS_NPU branch as a compile-time False constant via AST, then cut the exact line ranges out of the original text so comments and formatting survive byte-for-byte.
Delete modules whose entire subject is Ascend (AscendC GDN, MC2, TorchAIR, MindSpeed setup, the pinned core17 lock) after verifying each carries Ascend markers.

Compare against a separate git worktree at the pre-removal commit. The live tree is never mutated by the comparison (an earlier `git stash` round-trip on the shared tree was the wrong tool and produced one misread result).

outcome_changes_for_tests_present_in_bot.tests/test_document_packing.py::test_mco: SKIPPED -> PASSED: it pointed at the Ascend-only .deps/core17/Megatron-LM checkout, which never exists on CUDA, so it was vacuously skipped. It now parses the real installed megatron.core.distributed and actually exercises the hook contract.

tests.failure_in_both_trees: tests/test_wan_unified.py (pre-existing pyarrow/NumPy clash, reproduced identically on the pre-removal commit)

numerics.config: synthetic, seq 8192, tp1 dp2, GA1, bf16-grad-reduce, seed 42, 6 steps
numerics.verdict: Neutral. Run-to-run self-drift exceeds the cross-tree drift, so the difference is nondeterministic reduction order (CUDA atomics in the CQ event index_add_/scatter_add_, plus NCCL), not a changed code path. Step 1 is bit-identical across trees; divergence only appears after the first optimizer update, which is the signature of accumulated atomics.
numerics.confirmed_by_inspection: diff of ops/functional.py shows every removed line sits inside the `if ops:` NPU branch or an NPU-only autograd class; the surviving CUDA code is textually unchanged.

config_keys_deliberately_kept.PRETRAIN_ATTENTION_TILE: 2048 still drives CPU query tiling for the dense fallback
config_keys_deliberately_kept.PRETRAIN_COMPILE_MODULATION: 0; the Inductor DiT pointwise fusion measured slower

behaviour_change_on_purpose: PRETRAIN_STACK=core17 now raises instead of silently resolving to the CUDA lock. utils/dependencies.py always promised never to fall back to another stack silently.
